slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: AWS access without keys
slides.subtitle: How a workshop problem became useful for coding agents too.

slides.title: The workshop constraint
slides.body: I needed 50 or 60 people to provision AWS resources from their own machines. No keys to copy. Nothing to install. No access to my main AWS account.

slides.title: The credential endpoint
slides.body: A Lambda assumes an AWS role and returns temporary credentials. The AWS SDK fetches them through AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI.

slides.title: Why this matters
slides.body: Long-lived keys are hard to control once they leave your machine. Temporary credentials give you a way to scope, expire, and revoke access.

slides.title: Same pattern for agents
slides.body: Coding agents can experiment in a sandbox AWS account without getting permanent access or a path to production.

slides.supportingText: The System I Built for AWS Access Without Keys.
